name: Student reasoning classifier
summary: A BERT classifier from Stanford that finds a student's turn in which they explain their mathematical reasoning, trained on annotations of 4th and 5th grade math lessons (the NCTE transcripts).
grades: not stated (trained on 4th and 5th grade math lessons)

license.note: Its card's metadata says GPL and names no version, and the card holds nothing else. GPL sets the terms for passing a work on, so ask its authors which version they mean before you share it or anything built from it.

access_note: About 440 MB, not gated. Edu-ConvoKit 0.4.0 calls it ddemszky/student-reasoning, which now leads here; the NCTE repository points to Edu-ConvoKit to run it.
cite: Demszky, D., & Hill, H. (2023). The NCTE Transcripts: A Dataset of Elementary Math Classroom Transcripts. BEA 2023, 528-538. https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2023.bea-1.44

fits.how: Marks the turns where the learner explains their reasoning: the Edu-ConvoKit component runs it on messages of 8 words or more, on the person's own computer, once they download it.

connect.note: Runs in the Edu-ConvoKit component's detector (edu-convokit) once you download it yourself. Its license is unclear, so nothing here fetches it. Trained on spoken classroom talk; nobody has checked it on chats with an AI.
